chapters.title: Hiragana: M, Y, R, W, N

lessons.title: Voiced sounds: が and ざ rows
lessons.authorNote: Teach the change as one rule on shapes the learner already knows, with one kana card per sound and no itemId on any card. The lesson targets are the words, never a base kana. Read every target word in the Teach beat, and write the sound in rōmaji only in the cards. The rule here: two small marks turn か into が and さ into ざ.

lessons.title: Voiced sounds: だ, ば and ぱ rows
lessons.authorNote: Teach the change as one rule on shapes the learner already knows, with one kana card per sound and no itemId on any card. The lesson targets are the words, never a base kana. Read every target word in the Teach beat, and write the sound in rōmaji only in the cards. The rule here: two small marks voice た and は, a small circle turns は into ぱ. Say that ぢ and づ are rare and sound like じ and ず.

lessons.title: Combination sounds: きゃ, しゅ, ちょ
lessons.authorNote: Teach the change as one rule on shapes the learner already knows, with one kana card per sound and no itemId on any card. The lesson targets are the words, never a base kana. Read every target word in the Teach beat, and write the sound in rōmaji only in the cards. The rule here: a small ゃ, ゅ or ょ after an い-column kana makes one sound. Show the cards once, quickly: most of them are only for recognising, and the five target words carry the practice.

lessons.title: Long vowels
lessons.authorNote: Teach through the five target words, with no cards. Explain that a held vowel takes two beats and changes the word, and that えい usually sounds like a long え and おう like a long お. There is no audio yet, so describe the timing in words, for example clapping twice. Read every target word in the Teach beat.

lessons.title: The small っ pause
lessons.authorNote: Teach the change as one rule on shapes the learner already knows, with one kana card per sound and no itemId on any card. The lesson targets are the words, never a base kana. Read every target word in the Teach beat, and write the sound in rōmaji only in the cards. The rule here: a small っ is a short silent beat before the next sound. There is no audio yet, so describe the beat in words.

lessons.title: Reading real words with every sound
lessons.authorNote: The learner reads every target word and types how it sounds, with no rōmaji in the prompt. Use only the sounds taught in this chapter.

lessons.title: Hello and goodbye
lessons.authorNote: For every phrase, say when to say it and to whom, not only what it means. Each phrase gets a short real situation. At least one check gives a situation and asks which phrase fits. Phrases are learned whole: do not break them into grammar. Situations: time of day, arriving, leaving and going to bed.

lessons.title: Thank you and sorry
itemIds: ja:vocab:ありがとうございます
lessons.authorNote: For every phrase, say when to say it and to whom, not only what it means. Each phrase gets a short real situation. At least one check gives a situation and asks which phrase fits. Phrases are learned whole: do not break them into grammar. Situations: thanking a friend or a stranger, getting someone's attention, apologising, and answering thanks.

lessons.title: Yes, no and please
lessons.authorNote: For every phrase, say when to say it and to whom, not only what it means. Each phrase gets a short real situation. At least one check gives a situation and asks which phrase fits. Phrases are learned whole: do not break them into grammar. Situations: answering yes or no, offering something and asking for something.

lessons.title: Meeting someone

lessons.authorNote: For every phrase, say when to say it and to whom, not only what it means. Each phrase gets a short real situation. At least one check gives a situation and asks which phrase fits. Phrases are learned whole: do not break them into grammar. Situations: meeting someone for the first time and asking how someone is.

lessons.title: At the table and in the shop
lessons.authorNote: For every phrase, say when to say it and to whom, not only what it means. Each phrase gets a short real situation. At least one check gives a situation and asks which phrase fits. Phrases are learned whole: do not break them into grammar. Situations: before and after a meal, entering a shop, asking for something and asking someone to repeat.

chapters.title: Katakana: H through ン, and its sounds

lessons.title: Katakana sounds: ー, ッ, ャ and voiced marks
lessons.authorNote: Teach ー, ッ, small ャ and the voiced marks as the same rules the learner met in hiragana, with one card each. Lesson targets are the words. No foreign-sound combinations such as ティ or ファ.

lessons.title: Is not: じゃありません
There is (people, animals): がいます
Polite verbs: ます
lessons.authorNote: Teach ます only for the verbs the learner already knows from the last three lessons, with no conjugation table.

lessons.title: Do not: ません
lessons.authorNote: Teach ません only for the verbs the learner already knows, and include わかりません as "I don't understand".

lessons.title: Did: ました
lessons.authorNote: Teach ました only for the verbs the learner already knows, with no conjugation table.

lessons.title: The て-form
lessons.authorNote: This is the hardest point in the slice. Teach the て-form only for verbs the learner already knows, as a short list, with no complete table. Its only use for now is before ください, which is the next lesson.

lessons.title: Please do: てください
lessons.authorNote: Use only the て-forms taught in the last lesson.

lessons.title: I like: がすきです
lessons.authorNote: Write すき in kana: its kanji is never taught in this course.

lessons.title: I want to: たいです
lessons.authorNote: Do not use the word "stem" in learner-facing text. Say what goes before たいです by showing the ます form without ます.

lessons.title: Full self-introduction
itemIds: ja:vocab:よろしくおねがいします
lessons.authorNote: Practise the whole self-introduction: greeting, name, where you are from, what you do, something you like, and a closing phrase.

lessons.title: Writing your introduction
itemIds: ja:vocab:よろしくおねがいします
lessons.authorNote: End with one open check: answerType "typed", grading "open", no choices. The learner writes a short self-introduction with no hints and no link to an earlier lesson. correctAnswer is a model answer in kana. The rubric lists the six parts (greeting, name, where they are from, what they do, something they like, a closing phrase) and accepts any reasonable content, including the learner's own name in rōmaji.
